# Module delivery and live update boundaries — research plan

Observed: 2026-11-22, Europe/Kiev. Parent repository source starts at
`7d9c6ab06b296feb286dcf0c6edb510be8ac4105`; current organization guidance is
`0b44c64c824f536bd1b085341e7669bcc64ef124`.

## Authorized scope and decision discipline

The owner requests deeper Module Federation and adjacent industry research,
architecture preparation and verified findings. Contested runtime, sharing,
restart, delivery and state policies remain open. Recommendations must name
alternatives and the evidence that favors them; no recommendation becomes an
accepted public contract. Previously accepted TS-first library direction,
existing mechanism owners and canonical state authority remain in force.

## Parallel investigations

| Lane | Questions | Owned mechanism boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Federation | Actual shared-instance selection, forced registration, cache/reference behavior, generated remote identity, failure during preparation | Existing webpack/Rspack/Module Federation loader and runtime; no substitute loader |
| Desktop | Renderer, preload bridge, main, utility process, native addon and packaged application update scopes | Electron/Node lifecycle, IPC and updater; actual resource and authority owners |
| Web delivery | Import-map resolution, SystemJS relinking, lifecycle helpers, service-worker takeover, old lazy assets and document/realm state | Browser, existing module loaders, Workbox/deployer mechanisms |
| Root synthesis | Dependency-ordered rollout, readiness/acknowledgement semantics, object replacement, invariant/choice split and owner questions | Existing Get Modular plans, Resources, product grants/state and narrow adapters |

## Work and review sequence

1. Read existing authority and prior evidence; preserve its original identities.
2. Record primary sources, current release versus development-head differences,
   exact source pins, positive guarantees and specific limitations.
3. Commit and immediately push an initial research checkpoint.
4. Review any bounded native experiment before implementation and again before
   execution; use strict TypeScript >=7.0.2 and real published mechanisms.
5. Retain original failures separately. Do not rerun unchanged older E2E or
   count source inspection as executed behavior.
6. Critique the combined architecture from dependency, failure, state, trust,
   delivery and user-control perspectives. Turn unsupported claims into open
   qualification cases, not additional speculative subsystems.
7. Present a small prioritized set of owner questions with 2–3 alternatives,
   the preferred option and remaining uncertainty. Preserve these in OD-003.
8. Run the repository documentation gate; audit actual final-head checks and
   carry forward only byte-identical qualified native inputs.

## Proportional estimates

These are planning judgments, not measured reliability. This investigation
introduces **zero production/library LOC** and no public API.

| Work | Integration/production LOC | Fixture/test LOC | Complexity /10 | Reliability in bounded scope /10 | Confidence /10 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Source-backed reports and decision alternatives | 0 | 0 | 4 | N/A | 8 |
| Potential generated-remote Federation experiment | 0 | 450–850 | 5 | 8 | 7 |
| Potential released SystemJS semantics experiment | 0 | 220–380 | 3 | 8 | 7 |
| New Electron/Envoy/Unreal runtime execution | 0 | 0 planned | N/A | Unqualified | N/A |

Fixture bounds are incremental, conditional on a question that can change the
choice, and exclude CI/release maintenance. These are not estimates of the
complete standalone library. A public architecture cannot guarantee that all
future refactoring disappears; the target is explicit variation points backed
by concrete alternatives and avoided coupling.

## Expected outputs

Governed research synthesis, exact source/findings ledgers, named reuse warnings,
review dispositions, optional frozen native inputs/results, owner alternatives
and a portable supplement to the prior standalone packet. Root alone changes
the repository, commits and pushes. Native production adoption and merge remain
outside this research checkpoint.

# Module Federation: research and bounded native qualification plan

Status: **REVIEW REQUIRED — no native fixture implemented or executed.**
Date: 2026-11-22. Owner: `/root/mf_runtime`. This directory is research evidence; root owns repository integration, commits and pushes. It does not select a production runtime, public API, isolation or migration policy.

## Questions that can change architecture

1. Which identities are actually distinct: remote registration name, entry global, webpack `output.uniqueName`, module factory/export reference, share-scope object and selected shared singleton? Which survive a forced registration?
2. Does loading a candidate already execute plugin code before an application publishes it? Which lower-level factory deferral is available, and what remains executable before that boundary?
3. Can a failed forced replacement destroy the old registration while existing old references still work? This separates runtime lookup from application selection and resources.
4. When is a shared singleton an identity requirement (JupyterLab service tokens), and what does an incompatible version do under strict and non-strict policies?
5. Does a fresh runtime instance isolate a previously initialized webpack container? The generated init guard compares share-scope object identity.
6. What do real consumers, HMR and SSR establish, and what do they leave to the application?

## Source plan

- Pin released implementations: MF runtime/core 2.9.3 / `40688424f13ea9d4338b9a0cf230e8f1ac4d3835`; webpack 5.113.0 / `e9f0c9b25456ae5d80739ba7f498ae5b623ca194`; compare the documented Rspack 2.3.3 family without pretending it is the same implementation.
- Inspect JupyterLab 4.6.6 / `8d57791d0254820dfa4a540e010105803e128bcd` as an operational consumer: prebuilt package versus plugin unit, token identity, dependency sharing and loading.
- Separate current source observations, documentation promises, historical issue reports and native reproductions. The prior F01/F10 investigation and historical MF verdict are context, not fresh native evidence.
- Check positive guarantees: working compatible singleton sharing, supported factory deferral, genuine generated-container initialization, and versioned artifact coexistence where observed. Do not label all sharing or all caching a failure.

## Proposed one native spike: actual generated containers + published runtime

**Profile:** Chromium browser, a same-origin disposable HTTP fixture, webpack's actual `container.ModuleFederationPlugin` 5.113.0 generating script containers, and published `@module-federation/runtime` 2.9.3 in a generated host bundle. No enhanced bundler plugin, Rspack native binding, HMR server, React, synthetic container, custom MF loader or production library changes. This is a narrow interoperability profile, not proof for MF-enhanced/Rspack/Electron/SSR.

Maintained inputs are `.ts`. `typescript@7.0.2` checks/emits them with `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `useUnknownInCatchVariables`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, `skipLibCheck:false`. Webpack consumes the emitted JavaScript as build output; emitted container/runtime JS is an upstream/generated artifact, not maintained application code. `node:test` and `playwright@1.65.1` exercise the actual browser. Node types pinned at `@types/node@24.13.3`.

### Compiler/dependency gate before any native execution

The proposed direct pins are webpack 5.113.0, MF runtime 2.9.3, TypeScript 7.0.2, Playwright 1.65.1 and Node types 24.13.3. Registry manifests already show that runtime -> runtime-core/sdk/error-codes 2.9.3 has no TypeScript compiler dependency. Webpack direct dependencies have none; transitive resolution is **not yet audited**. The enhanced package is deliberately outside this fixture because its declaration tooling is irrelevant to these questions.

After plan approval, resolve an isolated lockfile with install scripts disabled; inspect every resolved package for TypeScript/compiler dependencies and embedded compiler files before `tsc`, webpack or the browser runs. Record exact lock hash and packages. Stop if any compiler below 7.0.2 would execute. Verify compiler version from the selected executable and use existing installed browser binaries where available. A dependency problem causes a plan amendment, never a silent compiler downgrade.

### Frozen proposed test matrix

| ID | Native operation | Decisive observable assertions | Positive control / limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| MF-N1 | Load A, retain its exported object and explicitly installed listener; force same registration to a distinct generated B entry/global/uniqueName; load B | New lookup returns B; retained A object still returns A; A listener remains until its explicit cleanup. Candidate B top-level marker appears during `loadRemote`, before fixture publication. | B is genuinely generated and executes; explicit cleanup removes A listener. This is not a GC/unload or security test. |
| MF-N2 | Load A; keep an unrelated registered remote with an alias prefix that conflicts with the proposed forced replacement; force replacement of A with that invalid alias | Native `registerRemotes(...,{force:true})` throws after its removal branch; inspect registered names and subsequent lookup; retained A callable and already-installed A resource remain observable. | Use source-confirmed alias validation, not a fabricated runtime exception. Do not conclude every failure has this order. |
| MF-N3 | A generated container with a shared fixture service-token package; first resolve compatible singleton, then attempt a distinct generated consumer requiring incompatible singleton with strict policy | Compatible consumer receives identical token reference; strict incompatible consumer rejects. Record selected provider/version and error. Optionally non-strict counterpart only if within LOC budget. | Real shared package and actual webpack-generated consume runtime. Semver compatibility does not prove business protocol/state compatibility. |
| MF-N4 | Two MF runtime instances target the same already-initialized generated container in the same browser realm, each with its own share-scope map; compare fresh browser context | Same-realm container rejects a different scope object through native generated init guard; fresh context succeeds. | New MF instance is not a realm. Do not assert that independent MF instances always share every map. |

N1 can additionally obtain `loadRemote(...,{loadFactory:false})` on a fresh remote if supported by the exact public typings: distinguish entry/get/init effects from exposed factory execution. It must not become a fabricated side-effect-free transaction. This control is bounded to a single extra assertion and is omitted with an explicit reason if it requires unsupported internals.

Lazy-chunk/CDN retention and startup strategy outage remain source-backed questions here; the delivery research owns the broader asset-closure probes. No existing project E2E suite is rerun.

## Implementation/review budgets

- Production code: **0 LOC**. Public API changes: **0**. Repository/workflow changes by this agent: **0**.
- Maintained disposable TypeScript: target 450–700 LOC; hard review trigger above 850 LOC. Count build/server/browser runner separately from remote/host fixture inputs.
- Complexity estimate: **5/10**; mostly generated-bundle setup and exact scope semantics. Reliability of the bounded test design: **8/10** once positive controls pass. Current confidence before native execution: **7/10**. These are engineering judgments, not measured availability.
- Freeze the matrix after root and peer critique. A source observation alone must not be relabeled native evidence. If one case cannot be built using released APIs, report the limitation rather than emulate MF semantics.
- Native receipts must include commands, Node/browser/compiler versions, dependency audit, output/artifact hashes, assertions, and explicit applicability limits.

## Open decisions are outputs, not defaults

Surface to the owner: shared platform identity versus dependency-per-generation isolation; allowed update unit when shared singletons change; same-realm execution versus replaceable realm; startup availability tradeoff of share strategy; candidate evaluation authority; development HMR versus controlled production replacement; version/support/asset retention. No branch is adopted in this research.

# Desktop update boundary research

Status: source investigation; checkpoint 1, 2026-11-22 UTC. No runtime adoption or native Electron execution.

## Scope and evidence

Investigate Electron renderer, preload/contextBridge, IPC, utilityProcess, native add-ons and packaged application update boundaries. Integrate with the existing library blueprint; do not repeat prior Worker/CodeMirror experiments. Inspect official current docs and exact released source; distinguish source conclusions from executed observations. Owner decides trust profiles, restart policies and supported host contracts.

Baseline: extension-foundation `7d9c6ab06b296feb286dcf0c6edb510be8ac4105`; org quality standard `0b44c64c824f536bd1b085341e7669bcc64ef124`. Current Electron release discovered 2026-11-22: `v45.4.1`, published 2026-11-19, commit `deaded07eebdfe9a3737884933b1acbe65971f64`, with Chromium `156.0.8078.100` and Node `v24.22.3` in DEPS. These pins scope conclusions; future upgrades need renewed verification.

3. Separate native ABI, binary replacement, ASAR integrity and application updater responsibilities; review specific upstream incidents and counterevidence.
4. Publish capability/update-scope table, architecture constraints, open owner questions, source ledger and evidence gaps.

# Electron and desktop live-update boundaries

Checkpoint 1 — 2026-11-22. Source research only; no native Electron execution. Existing research is reused, not counted as new evidence.

## Early verified findings

1. Electron `v45.4.1` is pinned to `deaded07eebdfe9a3737884933b1acbe65971f64`. `contextBridge` copies/freezes non-function values by default and proxies functions. Released source rejects binding a second API over an existing window property. Updating renderer code therefore does not replace the installed preload contract. A proxied method may still delegate to mutable internal behavior; a frozen surface does not mean all behavior is immutable.
2. `session.registerPreloadScript` runs for relevant new contexts; docs explicitly exclude rerunning it during in-page navigation. Registry removal does not document reversal of already executed code. Treat code publication, context creation and effect cleanup as separate operations.
3. IPC handler registration and already dispatched work are separate. Released `ipcMain.removeHandler` deletes a map entry; native dispatch attaches fulfillment/rejection callbacks to an existing returned promise. Removing the registration is not evidence that previous work stopped.
4. `utilityProcess.kill()` returns before observed process exit. Its exact released implementation also calls Chromium `EnsureProcessTerminated`; on non-Apple POSIX upstream Chromium uses a background reaper with a two-second wait and SIGKILL. Consequently, a simplistic reading of moving documentation as "SIGTERM only; can remain forever" is unsupported. Exact Electron patches and platform variants remain under inspection. Electron normalizes expected killed SIGTERM/SIGKILL exit codes to zero; zero alone does not prove guest finalizers ran.

## Scope boundary

Renderer Module Federation can load code into the renderer's execution environment, but cannot by itself replace an existing preload contract, already running main-process code, native binary, or packaged application. Main-owned resources may outlive renderer navigation. A later full report will map physical contexts and supported update actions without selecting an Electron execution profile for the library.

## Evidence limitations

These are documentation and source-inspection conclusions. No claimed Electron E2E, source-level concurrency proof, platform compatibility certification, or guarantee of zero future refactoring. References and owner questions are being expanded in this checkpoint.

# Owner questions — preliminary

No option is adopted by this research.

1. Is the desktop renderer plugin surface restricted to trusted first-party code, or must it accept independently supplied code? The answer changes which realm/process and authority boundary is appropriate; Module Federation loading alone does not answer it.
2. Should a stable preload/IPC protocol support multiple renderer plugin generations, or should incompatibility require a coordinated renderer/app restart? Recommendation to evaluate: explicit protocol compatibility plus an observable restart requirement; exact support window remains an owner choice.
3. Which resources must survive renderer refresh: drafts, device handles, sessions, native jobs? Their custodian must be outside the replaced context or state needs a verified checkpoint/recovery protocol. Custody placement remains a product decision.
4. Is native functionality eligible for a separately restarted utility process, or is it coupled to application lifetime? This affects native update granularity and exclusive-resource handover; it is not decided here.
5. Which distribution channels permit external plugin artifacts, and which changes must use the signed application updater? The source evidence separates these mechanisms; the product's distribution policy is not inferred.

# Web delivery and live module replacement — investigation plan

Observed: 2026-11-22. Research only; no production choice or public API is adopted.
Root owns repository documentation, commits and publication. This lane owns only
the `delivery` scratch directory.

## Questions that can change the architecture

1. Which browser/module-loader operations change future resolution, and which
   preserve existing namespaces, consumers, custom-element definitions or styles?
2. Can one published deployment selector guarantee a coherent graph to an old
   tab that loads a delayed chunk after a rollout? What remains a storage/asset
   retention obligation?
3. What does Service Worker installation, activation, control and `skipWaiting`
   actually guarantee across existing clients?
4. What ready mechanisms provide import-map publication, lifecycle intent,
   caching and update notifications without supplying application authorization,
   state migration or physical reclamation?
5. Which invariant follows from current accepted ownership, and which rollout,
   sharing, isolation, retention or reset policy needs the owner's decision?

## Evidence method

- Use normative HTML/Service Worker specifications, official implementation
  documentation and exact released SystemJS/single-spa source.
- Record retrieval date, exact version/commit where available, source class,
  counterevidence and limits. A reported incident is not a reproduced defect.
- Carry forward the previous single-spa timeout/unload findings, not count them
  as new execution. No previous native E2E is rerun in this lane.
- Review existing import-map-deployer and Workbox mechanisms before suggesting
  a custom deployment selector, service worker or notification subsystem.
- Proposed architecture stays in the decision matrix. No package installation,
  public interface or runtime choice is implied by a source finding.

## Candidate bounded native spike — superseded, NOT executed

One real-browser fixture could distinguish module resolution from current live
objects using the browser's native import maps and dynamic imports. Candidate
cases: merge a nonconflicting late import map; try to remap an already-resolved
specifier; retain an existing export while importing an explicitly new immutable
URL; change only an entry query while a relative dependency retains its URL.
An independent assertion must observe actual values/identities and requests.

This would exercise native browser semantics, not implement a substitute
loader. Maintained source and harness would be `.ts`, strictly checked with
TypeScript >=7.0.2. Any emitted browser JavaScript would be generated. Exact
browser/compiler/runner/lock/source identities and original failures would be
retained. The fixture must not be called Module Federation E2E.

The default recommendation for this lane is source inspection first. Run the
fixture only if an unresolved architecture claim needs empirical discrimination
after review; sibling Federation work may cover the same boundary more directly.
No native run is authorized by this plan alone. Root review prefers the released
SystemJS probe below. Native import-map cases are dropped because the normative
rules answer the question without another browser fixture.

## Plan v2: released SystemJS probe — requires root review before execution

SystemJS 6.15.1 at commit `17c238ec00cf7c4bcabcf3579f876513fcedba30`
returns a callback from successful registry deletion. After reimport, it reconnects
importer setters. Official API prose says Boolean, but DefinitelyTyped documents
`false | UpdateModuleFn`. Upstream PR #2020 intentionally introduced this in 2019.
This changes the reuse assessment enough to justify a narrow native qualification.

Use the actual published SystemJS Node loader; this is neither browser evidence
nor Module Federation/library E2E. Maintained harness, build script and fixtures
are strict `.ts`. TypeScript 7.0.2 emits ESM; Rollup 4.68.8 converts it to generated
System.register output with preserved modules. TS7 removed legacy System output,
so do not use an old compiler or a TypeScript bundler plugin.

Use public import/delete/has APIs, real generated modules and the published
declarations. No instantiate hook, manual registry, ambient module shim or
diagnostic suppression. Validate imported unknown values before use.

Replace the temporary module file A with generated B at the same URL, then
reimport after delete. This is a mechanism fixture, not a production mutable-asset
recommendation. A separate real gate module provides a started promise and release
function for top-level await; no sleep-based success condition.

| Case | Independent observations | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-01 completed delete/reimport/relink | Delete returns function; new namespace reads B; importer reads A before callback, B after; old namespace and captured function remain A | Not resource cleanup, graph HMR, browser behavior or state preservation |
| SYS-02 callback guard (may fold into SYS-01) | Invocation before replacement returns false; after replacement it rebinds; repeated call reports false | Not safe application rollback |
| SYS-03 pending evaluation | Delete returns false during signalled top-level await; release completes original import; deletion can succeed afterwards | Not cancellation or deadline enforcement |

Published source and historical #2286/#2291 are inspected without counting the
old issue as a newly reproduced defect. Sibling real MF profile keeps separate
counts. No production loader choice is adopted.
